Notes: The Pontifical of John Russell, bishop of Lincoln (1480–94), containing Excommunicatio II (f. 282b) and the Consecratio regis and reginae (ff. 195b, 207).

English Translation: Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS Rawlinson C 400
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Pontifical of Roger de Martival, bishop of Salisbury (1315–29), containing in the Consecratio regis the Sacramentum coronationis in the Kb form.

German Expansion: Duke of Northumberland zu Alnwick Castle
English Translation: Alnwick Castle, the Duke of Northumberland
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] A volume owned by the Duke of Northumberland in which a once separate part begins with Glanvill, followed in the same 14th-century hand (f. 99v) by ECf to c. 34,1a, of the adow class.

English Translation: Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS 190
Date (Liebermann): early 11th century; p. 364 another hand, 11th century; p. 418 f. late 11th century
Notes: An early 11th-century manuscript, mainly homiletic and canonistic, given by Leofric to Exeter Cathedral as 'Scriftboc on Englisc'; related to C, G, P. In other hands it adds Excommunicatio III (p. 364), the Confessionale and Poenitentiale Pseudo-Egberti, and at the end (late 11th century) Mirce, Að and Had, these taken from doi. It was copied in Harley 438.

English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Otho A.xvi
Notes: Cotton Otho A XVI, now burnt, which contained 'Leges Gul. conq.' — probably Wl art and/or ECf retr — together with the Genealogia Normannica to Stephen, i.e. the Tripartita.

English Translation: Oxford, Oriel College, MS 46
Laws in it: Quadr, Ine, Blas, Forf, Hu, Af, AGu, App AGu, EGu, I As, As Alm, II As, Episc, Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, IV As, V As, III As, VI As, Ordal, Iud Dei, Cn, Wl art retr, ECf retr, Lond ECf, Hn, CHn cor, Hn Lond
Notes: Written in one hand c. 1330, once owned by the London Guildhall and then by Francis Tate; a codex of the London Leges Anglorum (see Lond), mostly closer to Co than K, taking many insertions added in Co into its text; Gi mostly reads like Or. Contents: Expositio vocabulorum, Numerus provinciarum, Quadripartitus texts (Ine, Alfred, Æthelstan, etc.), Iudicium Dei XVI, I, XV, Cnut, then Tripartita (rubric list, Wl art retr, ECf retr with London interpolations, Genealogia Normannica), and Henry I's laws with his coronation and London charters.

English Translation: London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), Liber Ordinationum
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] The Liber ordinationum of the London Guildhall, containing (f. 161) the Libertas Londoniensis joined with the French Amplificator text.

German Expansion: Vita s. Oswaldi archiepiscopi Eboracensis, auct. monacho Rameseiensi
English Translation: The Life of St Oswald of York, by a monk of Ramsey
Notes: The Life of St Oswald of York by a Ramsey monk, composed 995–1005, which uses the Sacramentum coronationis.

German Expansion: Verlorene Vorlage von Ot und sq für II As
English Translation: Lost manuscript, reconstructed by Liebermann from its copies
Notes: [lost] Lost exemplar of Ot and sq for II Æthelstan.

German Expansion: British Museum Cotton Otho B XI
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Otho B.xi
Notes: Partly burnt; it once held the Old English Bede from Southwick, the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (printed by Wheloc; Lambarde's 1564 transcript is now in Dublin) and bishop lists to 1005/12. The remains (c. 1010), bound out of order, contain Alfred–Ine (rubrics and fragments), where Ot is close to E and seems copied from it, and also near l; and II Æthelstan 7–25 (cf. osq).

German Expansion: British Museum Cotton Otho A X
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Otho A.x (burnt in 1731; known from Wanley’s extract in Hickes, Thesaurus, 1705)
Notes: A medieval parchment manuscript, now burnt, containing IX Æthelred.

English Translation: Oxford, University College, MS 176
Notes: Copied c. 1570 from Lambarde's printed edition (Ld), faithfully reproducing its decorations, notes, headings and errors. Behind Af El it adds a second prologue in Alfred's name mentioning Asser, which Liebermann judges spurious, probably a 16th-century invention to exalt Asser and Oxford.

English Translation: Oxford, Corpus Christi College, MS 157
Notes: Manuscript of Florence of Worcester, containing Cnut's letter of 1027 (p. 329).

German Expansion: Paris, Bibliothèque nationale Lat. 10575 (früher Suppl. lat. 138)
English Translation: Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, MS lat. 10575 (formerly Suppl. lat. 138)
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Contains the Benedictio ignis, Capitula de sacerdotibus and Excarpsum de canonibus, then (ff. 7–172) the so-called Pontificale Egberti in a hand '200 years younger than Egbert', followed by an 11th-century ritual from Évreux, an Old English absolution formula (c. 1000), and after the coronation rite the Sacramentum coronationis (f. 137).

English Translation: Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, MS 6044
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] A 16th-century copy of Henry of Huntingdon with Instituta Cnuti, according to Arnold copied from Lb.

English Translation: Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, MS fr. 4901
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Collectanea of Toustain de Billy (c. 1700), with a few lines of the Leis Willelme copied from Isp.

English Translation: Peterborough Cathedral, Swaffham’s Register
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Swaffham's Register at Peterborough Cathedral, containing (f. 277) the Tripartita, i.e. Wl art, ECf retr and the Genealogia Normannica to 1154. Derived with Hy from pehy.

English Translation: Cambridge, University Library, MS 3392 (formerly Phillipps 8079)
Notes: Contains Henry of Huntingdon to 1147, then the Tripartita (Wl art, ECf retr, Genealogia Normannica) and Huntingdon's De summitatibus.

English Translation: Phillipps MS 26641 (formerly 2777)
Laws in it: Wl lad, Praef ad CHn cor
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] William of Malmesbury's Gesta regum with Ip Ml, i.e. Wl lad and the preface to Henry I's coronation charter.

German Expansion: Phillipps 8078, dann H. S. Nichols & Co. zu London
English Translation: Phillipps MS 8078 (in 1903 owned by H. S. Nichols & Co., London)
Laws in it: ECf, Lib Lond, In Cn, Wl art
Notes: Written c. 1300, at Phillipps's until 1895, then owned by H. S. Nichols & Co., London. In the starred pieces it agrees with S but sometimes reads better, so it derives from sp: ECf, Libertas Londoniensis, Instituta Cnuti, Huntingdon's 'Chnutus rex cum XX annis', the Tripartita (Wl art, Genealogia Normannica to John), De longitudine Anglie, Glanvill and other pieces. Per f. 25 the exemplar of Pl and S followed the Ip Hunt class for In Cn and Tripartita.

English Translation: Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, MS 943
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Pontifical for Sherborne, perhaps given there by Dunstan, with Old English pieces, in France from the late 11th century. Contains Sherborne documents and letters, the Consecratio regis, reginae with the Sacramentum coronationis (f. 67), Iudicium Dei I–III (ff. 89b–95b), the Excerptio de canonibus Egberti, and a 12th-century book list.

German Expansion: Pithou's Druck (Franc. Pithoeus Gloss. ad Capitul., 1588)
English Translation: Pierre Pithou, glossary to the Capitularies (1588), printed
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Pithou's printed edition of the Iudicium Dei, according to Rozière taken from Ps.

German Expansion: British Museum Cotton Vespasianus D XV
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Vespasian D.xv
Date (Liebermann): f. 3b c. 1130; partly 11th century; f. 84–101 c. 1000
Notes: Excommunicatio XII on a flyleaf (f. 3b, c. 1130), followed by a partly 11th-century benedictional and Old English and theological material, of which ff. 84–101 (c. 1000) agree with Thorpe, Ancient laws p. 307.

German Expansion: British Museum Regius 11 B II (Liber monasterii Wygornie)
English Translation: London, British Library, Royal MS 11 B II (Liber monasterii Wygornie)
Laws in it: Quadr, I Cn, II Cn, Af, Ine, I As, II As, Ordal, Episc, Norðleod, Geþyncðo, Mirce, Að, Had, Blas, Forf, Hu, IV As, VI As, EGu, II Em, Swer, Wif, Wer, III Atr, Pax, Wal, IV Atr, II Atr, Duns, Iudex, Rect, Wl lad
Notes: Worcester book written c. 1160 handsomely but thoughtlessly, often keeping e-caudata for ae; ff. 103–166 hold the middle recension of the Quadripartitus from Arg. 32 (Cnut, Alfred–Ine, Æthelstan, Edgar, Edmund, Æthelred and the shorter tracts, to Wl lad), followed in the same hand by Odo of Cambrai's De canone missae. R was copied in Lh.

English Translation: London, British Library, Royal MS 13 A XVIII
Notes: After Henry of Huntingdon, the Tripartita with Rubricator II (Wl art, like Vi changing the title to plural majesty; cf. rv), the rubric list to ECf, ECf retr and the Genealogia Normannica to 1154; English history continued as in Gr to 1232, and finally the same verses as in Lb.

English Translation: London, British Library, Royal MS 13 C II
Laws in it: In Cn, Wl art, ECf retr
Notes: In Henry of Huntingdon, Instituta Cnuti (ff. 108–19); after Huntingdon the Tripartita with Rubricator II (Wl art, rubric list to ECf, ECf retr, Genealogia Normannica to 1154), then the verses as in Lb.

German Expansion: Regino De synodalibus causis II 414. 416 f., ed. Wasserschleben p. 373 ff.
English Translation: Regino of Prüm, De synodalibus causis II 414, 416 f. (ed. Wasserschleben, p. 373)
Notes: Regino of Prüm's De synodalibus causis (ed. Wasserschleben), source of Excommunicatio I and II.

English Translation: Rouen, Bibliothèque municipale, MS 368 (A 27)
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Pontifical in Frankish minuscule for south English Benedictines, later owned by Lan Aleth (Brittany, later Saint-Malo) and then Jumièges. Its coronation liturgy (ed. Legg) has the Sacramentum coronationis; ff. 159–175 have Iudicium Dei IX, II and I–III with Old English gloss, most closely related to Ch, Vt; also Egbert's Poenitentiale and, on f. 183 (not part of the original volume), an excommunication by the bishop of Alet, partly collated as Alet. Cf. Ro.

English Translation: Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS Rawlinson C 641
Laws in it: ECf, In Cn, CHn cor, Wl art
Notes: In a French hand c. 1185, preserving the diphthong æ at ECf 35,1d; ff. 3–10 ECf. After laws of 1166, 1170, 1215 etc., a hand of c. 1200 adds Instituta Cnuti, Henry I's coronation charter and Wl art, for which Rl stands closest to H (see hrl).

English Translation: Rouen, Bibliothèque municipale, MS 369 (Y 7)
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Benedictional and pontifical of the late 10th century from Newminster, Winchester, for its abbot Æthelgar (later bishop of Selsey and archbishop of Canterbury), formerly owned by Archbishop Robert of Canterbury, then Rouen Cathedral; f. 162 Consecratio regis with the Sacramentum coronationis. Cf. Rj.

English Translation: Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155
Notes: Robertson’s siglum (1925), not Liebermann’s; her base text for Wl art retr and Hn Lond.

German Expansion: Verlorene Vorlage von Ra und Vi
English Translation: Lost manuscript, reconstructed by Liebermann from its copies
Notes: [lost] Lost exemplar of Ra and Vi for the Tripartita.

German Expansion: London, Public Record Office, Transcripts for the new edition of Rymer's Foedera, 158 Rome III D 2
English Translation: London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), transcripts for the new edition of Rymer’s Foedera, 158 Rome III D 2
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Transcript made for the new edition of Rymer's Foedera, copied from Va.

English Translation: Lost manuscript, reconstructed by Liebermann from its copies
Notes: [lost] The exemplar used for Rymer's Foedera (ed. 1816, I 3) for William's episcopal-courts writ.

German Expansion: London, Public Record Office, Transcripts for Rymer's Foedera, 158 IV D 3
English Translation: London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), transcripts for Rymer’s Foedera, 158 IV D 3
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Greith's transcript from Vc, among the Public Record Office transcripts for Rymer's Foedera.

English Translation: London, British Library, Harley MS 746
Laws in it: ECf, Lib Lond, Leis Wl, CHn cor, In Cn, Wl art
Notes: Parchment, ff. 4–104 c. 1325; in the starred pieces it derives with Pl from a common exemplar sp. Contains Glanvill, ECf (with rubrics from ECf retr), Libertas Londoniensis, the Latin Leis Willelme from L, Henry I's coronation charter, 13th-century laws, Registrum brevium, De longitudine Anglie, Instituta Cnuti, Huntingdon's 'Chnutus rex' (placing S in the Ip Hunt class) and from the Tripartita Wl art and the Genealogia Normannica continued to John. S was copied in Vl and Harley 785.

German Expansion: Scaccarii liber rubeus im Public Record Office zu London
English Translation: London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
Laws in it: Hn, Wl art Lond retr, Quadr, Wl lad, CHn cor, Hn mon, Hn com
Notes: The Red Book of the Exchequer, a collection compiled and corrected by the Exchequer official Alexander of Swereford (d. 1246), edited by Hall. Contains Leges Henrici (ff. 16–29b, c. 1225, corrected by Swereford), a tract on hides and the three law districts, financial pieces and the Dialogus de scaccario, and c. 1230 Wl art Lond retr and from the Quadripartitus Wl lad, CHn cor, Hn mon, Hn com and the Concordia of Stephen and Henry (1153). This part was copied in K3 and later Cambridge Trinity O 10, 20, the whole volume in Hg (1252); Hn was copied from it in Harley 311, Cambridge Dd VI 38 and Harley 785.

German Expansion: Mag. Sinicius camerarius pape (Liber censuum eccl. Rom.)
English Translation: The Liber censuum of the Roman Church (sentences brought by Master Sinicius, papal chamberlain, 1267)
Notes: Master Sinicius, papal chamberlain and nuncio in England, brought to the Curia in 1267 sentences on Peter's Pence from Instituta Cnuti (Ip Hunt class: I Cn Pr., 11) and ECf 10; they stand in the Liber censuum of the Roman church, in Vatican MS Christina reg. 451 (17th century) and in Vc.

English Translation: John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] John Selden's manuscript of the London Leges Anglorum (see Lond), containing Leges Henrici and Henry I's London charter, known from variants noted by Twysden (in Wheloc's Archaionomia 1644); it stands closest to K.

English Translation: London, British Library, Sloane MS 754
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] 16th-century manuscript containing (f. 1) William's and Henry I's London charters.

German Expansion: Canterbury Cathedral library B 2 n. 8 (Papierheft mit William Somner's Abschrift)
English Translation: Canterbury, Cathedral Library, B 2 no. 8 (William Somner’s transcript, 17th century)
Laws in it: Af, Ine, II As, II Eg, III Eg
Notes: A separately foliated paper booklet with William Somner's transcript of Anglo-Saxon laws, incomplete and misbound (after 1705 the Pseudo-Evangelium Nicodemi was bound behind it); it preserves Af to 38, Ine from 54, II As 1–15 and II Eg 4–III Eg 7,2, from an exemplar that did not have these gaps; the source is unnamed. For Eg it follows with Ld a lost ls (which with G follows a lost gls, perhaps direct from the original); for II As it derives, against H B (Ld), from sq; for Af–Ine it follows ls and gls.

English Translation: Henry Spelman, Concilia (1639) I 619, printed from his own manuscript
Notes: Spelman's Concilia prints from his own manuscript parts of ECf retr (Prol.–12, 12,5, 13,1, 15, 20–20,5, 23, 32); at p. 219 he takes 32b,3–8 only from Ld.

German Expansion: Verlorene Vorlage von S und Pl
English Translation: Lost manuscript, reconstructed by Liebermann from its copies
Laws in it: ECf, Lib Lond, In Cn, Wl art
Notes: [lost] Lost exemplar of S and Pl for ECf (with rubrics from ECf retr), Libertas Londoniensis, Instituta Cnuti (Ip Hunt class) and the Tripartita (Wl art, Genealogia Normannica continued to John).

German Expansion: Gemeinsame Vorlage von So und Quadr. für II As
English Translation: Lost manuscript, reconstructed by Liebermann from its copies
Notes: [lost] Lost exemplar shared by So and the Quadripartitus for II Æthelstan (derived from osq).

German Expansion: Manuale ad usum eccl. Sarum, ed. Rouen 1506
English Translation: The Sarum Manual (printed, Rouen, 1506)
Notes: The printed Salisbury Manual (Rouen 1506), reprinted in Henderson's York manual (Surtees Society 63, 1875), containing the Duel.

English Translation: London, British Library, Stowe MS 414
Notes: Paper manuscript once owned by Francis Tate, with Pseudo-Cnut de foresta (f. 284); with Cii it goes back to a lost cis.

German Expansion: British Museum Cotton Titus A XXVII
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Titus A.xxvii
Laws in it: Quadr, Cn, Af, Ine, I As, II As, Episc, Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, Blas, Forf, Hu, IV As, V As, III As, VI As, Ordal, AGu, App AGu, EGu, I Ew, II Ew, I Em, II Em, Swer, Wif, Wer, I Atr, III Atr, Pax, Wal, IV Atr, II Atr, Duns, VII Atr, Iudex, II Eg, III Eg, III Em, Wl lad, Wl art, Geþyncðo, Rect, CHn cor, Hn com, In Cn
Notes: After Geoffrey of Monmouth, an originally separate volume in two hands of c. 1225: the first writes the Quadripartitus from Arg. 1 (Cnut, Alfred–Ine, Æthelstan, Edgar, Edmund, Æthelred and the shorter tracts, Wl lad, Wl art — probably not from Quadr — Quadr II Praef., CHn cor, Quadr II 4–18, Hn com); another hand adds Instituta Cnuti (related to Cb), then Marbod's poems on stones. It contains the texts Andreas Horn added to Co from a 'Liber S. Augustini Cant.', so Liebermann thinks T belonged to St Augustine's, Canterbury; Sir Simonds d'Ewes either owned T or a sister manuscript, from which Somner cited VII Atr and Iudex and Harley 596 was copied (exemplar called 'pervetusta').

English Translation: Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS Tanner 5
Notes: Pontifical of the Salisbury rite, with the Duel on p. 120.

English Translation: Cambridge, Trinity College, MS B 11, 10
Notes: 12th-century pontifical of the province of Canterbury, probably East Anglian, perhaps from Ely, with Iudicium Dei XI (p. 49) and XII (p. 110) and a Consecratio regis (p. 104); most closely related to Ll.

German Expansion: Verlorene Vorlage von T und Cb für In Cn
English Translation: Lost manuscript, reconstructed by Liebermann from its copies
Notes: [lost] Lost exemplar of T and Cb for the Instituta Cnuti.

German Expansion: British Museum Cotton Tiberius C I, f. 42–201
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Tiberius C.i, f. 42–201
Notes: Pontifical for Salisbury (c. 1075), with an excommunication of 'Leo papa' (f. 197) followed by Excommunicatio I.

English Translation: London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), Town Clerk’s Office (the original writ)
Notes: The original of William I's London charter, kept in the Town Clerk's office of the Guildhall.

German Expansion: British Museum Cotton Tiberius B VIII
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Tiberius B.viii
Notes: Pontifical (ff. 1–33, c. 1150) for a suffragan of Canterbury, later owned by Glasgow; bound into it is a coronation order written in 1365 for Charles V of France after early Anglo-Saxon formulas; then again c. 1150 the Duel (f. 152v) and Iudicium Dei XI (with II 2–5,3), XII, XIII, XIV. Most closely related to Vt 2 and Mg.

German Expansion: Eine Sammlung dreier Stücke verschiedener Autoren
English Translation: The Tripartita: a collection of Wl art, ECf retr and the Genealogia Normannica
Notes: [lost] A collection of three pieces by different authors — Wl art, ECf retr and the Genealogia Normannica — compiled 1140 (probably 1154)–1159, possibly by the genealogist himself. Its oldest manuscript (c. 1160) is Cb; others include Cu, Db, Kn, Lm, Oh, pehy and the appendix added to Huntingdon before 1200 in Lb, rv (Ra, Vi), Gr, Rc, La, Va, sp (S, Vl, Pl), Additional 21088, Ba, Jo, Ct, Ph; from this appendix probably also Hv and Lond (K Co Or).

German Expansion: Roger Twysden, Ausgabe für Wheloc's Archaionomia (1644)
English Translation: Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
Notes: Roger Twysden's edition in Wheloc's Archaionomia (1644) used for Hn, CHn cor and Hn Lond a text of the Lond class, Co and Or–Gi family. What Schmid prints as Tw for Wl art retr comes not from Wheloc but from Wilkins, who admits mixing Wl art and Wl art retr, so perhaps no separate manuscript lies behind it.

English Translation: Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Reg. lat. 587
Laws in it: In Cn, Wl art, ECf retr
Notes: Paper; in Henry of Huntingdon the Instituta Cnuti (cf. Ip Hunt), and after Hunt. book XII the Tripartita (Wl art, rubric list, ECf retr, Genealogia Normannica) and the verses ending Lb, thus from the group Ra Rc Vi Gr. Copied in Ry in the 19th century.

English Translation: Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, MS Vat. lat. 3495
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Contains Sinicius' extracts (see Sin); copied in Rym.

German Expansion: British Museum, Cotton Vespasian D XI
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Vespasian D.xi
Notes: Contains Excommunicatio X (f. 108b).

German Expansion: British Museum, Cotton Vitellius A XIII
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Vitellius A.xiii
Notes: Contains the Tripartita (Wl art, rubric list, ECf retr, Genealogia Normannica to 1154); with Ra it goes back to rv.

German Expansion: British Museum, Cotton Vitellius E V
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Vitellius E.v
Laws in it: ECf, Lib Lond, Leis Wl, CHn cor, In Cn, Wl art
Notes: Bound out of order and badly burnt, copied in the 16th century partly by L. Nowell, entirely from S: ECf, Libertas Londoniensis, Latin Leis Willelme, CHn cor, Instituta Cnuti, Huntingdon VI, and from the Tripartita Wl art and the Genealogia Normannica (reaching to John); other pieces found in S also stood in Vl.

English Translation: Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Reg. lat. 946
Notes: [not seen by Liebermann] Gesta Francorum to 1165, Pseudo-Turpin and other histories (13th century), customary law of the church of Avranches in various 12th-century hands, and on an added leaf (f. 75b) X Æthelred of the 11th century.

German Expansion: British Museum, Cotton Vitellius D VII
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Vitellius D.vii
Laws in it: Iud Dei, IV Eg, Geþyncðo, Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had
Notes: 16th-century transcripts: Iudicium Dei from Ci, IV Edgar from C, and from 'Cradok' Geþyncðo, Norðleod, Mirce, Að and Had; also Þa halgan (f. 144).

German Expansion: British Museum, Cotton Vitellius A VII
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Vitellius A.vii (Vt, the first pontifical)
Notes: Badly burnt. Vt (= Cv), the first pontifical, from Wessex c. 1060 (litany suggests shortly before 1000), most closely related to Rj and Ch, has the Sacramentum coronationis (f. 1, copied in Ju) and Iudicium Dei IX, I–III, VI, VII. Vt 2, a second pontifical of c. 1130, has Iudicium Dei XI–XIV, related to Mg and Tr.

German Expansion: British Museum, Cotton Vitellius A VII
English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Vitellius A.vii (Vt 2, the second pontifical)
Notes: Badly burnt. Vt (= Cv), the first pontifical, from Wessex c. 1060 (litany suggests shortly before 1000), most closely related to Rj and Ch, has the Sacramentum coronationis (f. 1, copied in Ju) and Iudicium Dei IX, I–III, VI, VII. Vt 2, a second pontifical of c. 1130, has Iudicium Dei XI–XIV, related to Mg and Tr.

English Translation: London, British Library, Cotton MS Vitellius E.xvii
Notes: The so-called Benedict of Peterborough's Gesta Henrici II (f. 18, c. 1210), then Evesham local records of the 15th century, and on a flyleaf (f. 252v, 14th century) Excommunicatio XI.

English Translation: The Westminster version of the Coronation Charter of Henry I
Notes: [lost] The Westminster recension of Henry I's coronation charter, found in Gl, Lond, Hl, Cust, S, Vl and Cant.

German Expansion: Worcester, Dean and Chapter, Wigornense Registrum prioratus
English Translation: Worcester Cathedral, Dean and Chapter: Registrum prioratus (the priory register)
Notes: The Worcester priory register (c. 1260), with pieces from ECf retr on f. 16.

English Translation: Worcester Cathedral, Dean and Chapter, MS 87
Notes: Glanvill (c. 1300), then in the same hand ECf to 34,1b of the adow class, then Bracton. Ed 1 was copied from Wo.

English Translation: Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS Junius 121
Notes: From Worcester, c. 1065, much used by Thorpe for the ecclesiastical canons of Ancient Laws; as c. 7 of his so-called 'Polity' it has Episcopus (f. 13b). Copied in Harley 441.

German Expansion: York manual, von Henderson edirt (Surtees soc. 63, 1875)
English Translation: The York Manual, ed. W. G. Henderson (Surtees Society 63, 1875)
Notes: The York Manual as edited by Henderson from Cambridge Univ. Ee 4,19 (c. 1350), Lawson (1403), Bodley (c. 1410), York Chapter and Fothergill (c. 1425) manuscripts and two prints (1509, after 1516); p. 106 the Duel, p. 122 Excommunicatio XIII.

English Translation: York, Minster Library, Add. 1 (York Gospels)
Notes: The York Minster gospel book (c. 1025), followed by homilies of c. 1030–70 repeating passages from Æthelred and Cnut, then in the same hand on a flyleaf Cnut's letter of 1020.

English Translation: the Latin version
Laws in it: VI Atr, IV Eg, Leis Wl
Notes: After a citation, L names the Latin version that Liebermann prints beside the text: for VI Atr the Latin paraphrase in MS K (VI Atr Lat, which has its own pages in the laws database), for IV Eg and for Leis Wl their Latin translations. So VI Atr 2 L is clause 2 of the Latin paraphrase. Not to be confused with the manuscript L used by Thorpe for ECf retr.
